clue.text: Rallying, essentially, around one banner

indicators.note: the phrase for essentially is placed round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: per se is Latin for 'in itself', essentially
I is the Roman numeral for one
a banner is a flag

explanation.surface: At its heart, a rally of supporters gathers round a single banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts PER SE (Latin, 'in itself') round I and FLAG. 'Rallying' looks like political gathering, but here it is the old sense of teasing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally someone, in an older sense, is to banter or tease them, and light mocking banter is exactly that.

clue.text: Possible catch for fisherman's successor

explanation.surface: Something an angler might land, or whoever takes over from a fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pope is a small freshwater fish also called a ruffe; St Peter the fisherman was the first bishop of Rome, so each pontiff succeeds him.

clue.text: Bloody wonderful?

explanation.surface: An exclamation: bloody wonderful!
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked rare is still bloody inside, and rare also means uncommonly fine or excellent.

clue.text: State capital needed after I'm failing to show foresight

indicators.note: the state capital is wanted after the first piece, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
Providence is the capital of the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A traveller admits they never thought to look up a state capital before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvidence is a lack of prudent planning for the future, a failure to look ahead.

clue.text: Housemasters

parts.note: read not as schoolteachers in charge of a boarding house but as the masters of the House, peers of the upper chamber of Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: Peers sit in the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, so they are masters of that House.

clue.text: Great explosion engulfing a little fuel tank

indicators.note: the scrambled letters swallow up the other piece, surrounding it
an explosion blows the letters of the word great apart into a new order

parts.note: some means a little, a certain amount

explanation.surface: A huge blast swallows a small fuel store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' scrambles the first word and 'engulfing' wraps it round the synonym for 'a little'; 'Great' looks like an adjective but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large storage vessel for town gas, a fuel holder.

clue.text: Strap drawn back to administer blow

indicators.note: the strap's word is pulled backwards, read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a taws is a leather strap once used for punishment in Scottish schools

explanation.surface: A teacher pulls back a strap to deliver a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: TAWS, a Scottish punishment strap, read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to hit sharply, to deliver a smack.

clue.text: Met expert held in awe — at her mansion

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is in awe of a woman at her grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is short for meteorology, as in the Met Office, the UK weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster is an expert in meteorology, the study of the weather.

clue.text: Offender in France's long past his best? Right

parts.note: in French, très passé means very much past it, long past one's best

explanation.surface: A French criminal is described as well past his prime, quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase très passé, very faded, is followed by R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser commits an offence by entering land without permission, so is a wrongdoer.

clue.text: ARA. perhaps, contrived to find new means of expression

indicators.note: contrived means artificially put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An abbreviation is reworked in search of a fresh way to say something.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ARA and PERHAPS rearrange into the answer; the full stop is just disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate a passage in different words.

clue.text: Right time for the latest fashion

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Now is the moment for the newest style.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is all the rage is the current craze.

clue.text: Helpful piece of music

explanation.surface: A useful bit of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Being instrumental in something means helping to bring it about; an instrumental is a tune played without singing.

clue.text: Basis of safe seat MP's in — or has he changed?

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: An MP with a secure constituency wonders whether a colleague has switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe seat' suggests politics, but the seat is a rider's position in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding skill is what keeps a rider secure in the saddle.

clue.text: Lines set by one master

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA
a set is a position or placing

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster gives out lines as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools 'lines' are a punishment: writing a sentence out many times.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposition was the schoolroom name for such a written punishment exercise.

clue.text: Slow progress with things that are hard to get into room

indicators.note: the hard things are pushed inside the word for room

parts.note: room means space
nails, as in the phrase 'hard as nails'

explanation.surface: Moving slowly with awkward items that won't fit through a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' signals the container; 'things that are hard' points to the phrase 'hard as nails', not to difficult things.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at the speed of a garden mollusc is proverbial for being very slow.

clue.text: Beggar's confession of being beyond redemption

explanation.surface: A beggar admits to being past saving.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a hopeless admission, 'mend I can't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives by asking alms; split up, the letters make the admission 'mend I can't', I am unfixable.

clue.text: Chronicler knowing volume is in Italian

parts.note: arch means knowing, slyly aware

indicators.note: the volume and is go inside the word for Italian

parts.note: V is the symbol for volume

explanation.surface: A knowing historian says a book is written in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'knowing' here means sly or roguish, the adjective arch, not well-informed.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist keeps historical records, a keeper of chronicles.

clue.text: Times calls for conditions to be agreed

explanation.surface: A newspaper demands that conditions be settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic periods are terms; to call or name something is to term it; and the provisions of a deal are its terms.

clue.text: Girl gets a ring, as it happens

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
live means broadcast in real time, as it happens

explanation.surface: A woman is given an engagement ring, reported in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Issue clear-cut order about one

indicators.note: the reordered letters go around the piece for one
to order is to arrange, so these letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to publish a definite command concerning someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges CLEARCUT, and 'about' puts it round I, after its first C.
explanation.definitionFit: To circulate a document is to distribute it, to put it out.

clue.text: I'd messed about with science and its lethal chemicals

indicators.note: messed about with means fiddled with and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to fooling around in the lab with dangerous chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I'D, SCIENCE and ITS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: These are poisons used to kill bugs, toxic agents.

clue.text: Man embraces little girl, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the island's abbreviation wraps round the girl's name, holding it

parts.note: IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man
Di is a short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: A man hugs a small girl, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency, shortened to IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic expression or turn of phrase.

clue.text: Child who's unruly and aberrant? Nothing odd in that

indicators.note: keeping nothing from the odd positions leaves only the even-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child is described as aberrant, which is hardly surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of ABERRANT and B, R, A, T remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved youngster.

clue.text: Composer in time for audition

indicators.note: for audition means for hearing, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as in 'doing bird'

explanation.surface: A composer has a slot in a schedule of auditions.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer; 'doing bird' is British slang for serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Byrd wrote church music and keyboard works in Elizabethan England.

clue.text: I see a name here

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Someone spots a name on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: here is a name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, the Russian form of John.

clue.text: Like some family hiding at home, in ominous fashion

indicators.note: the family word conceals the other piece within it

parts.note: sisterly means like a sister, one kind of family member
in means at home

explanation.surface: A family member hides out at the house, in a menacing way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' signals the container; 'Like some family' wants a single adjective for a family relation, not a description of relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or suggesting evil, so the adverb means menacingly.

clue.text: Demand to work may be heard

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to knead is to work dough with the hands

explanation.surface: A requirement to work might be spoken aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEAD, to work dough, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a requirement, something called for.

clue.text: Inspired fake takes in expert, ultimately

indicators.note: the word for fake absorbs the other letter within it

parts.note: simulated means fake, imitation

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word expert

explanation.surface: A forgery fools a specialist in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' puts T, the last letter of 'expert', inside SIMULATED after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulated means roused or spurred on, as an inspired person is.
